checks.public_requirement: Each of backbone_rmsd.csv, core_ca_rmsd.csv, mass_weighted_rmsd.csv and resid_weighted_rmsd.csv exists at its declared path under the output root and parses as comma-separated text with exactly one header row and one data row per trajectory frame in increasing 0-based frame order. The header must be exactly the columns specified for that file. No ragged rows, no empty/missing fields, no nonfinite or unparseable numbers, no extra or missing rows, and no index column. The Frame column must equal the 0-based row position (integer-valued; representation such as '0' or '0.0' is accepted).

For every frame row, Backbone, CORE, LID and NMP (unweighted RMSD after unweighted global fitting on all backbone atoms, per the domain-group rule) equal the reference values under the numeric tolerance rule above, and Time (ns) is compared at absolute 1e-9 as the reader-assigned per-frame time value. Required output equals one entry per frame (neither a subset nor extra values).

For every frame row, CORE (unweighted RMSD of CORE-domain alpha carbons after optimal superposition of that set onto frame 0) equals the reference value under the numeric tolerance rule, with the same Time (ns) and Frame comparison as the other tables.

For every frame row, C-alphas, CORE, LID and NMP (mass-weighted: alpha-carbon fitting set weighted by atomic masses, domain backbone atoms weighted by atomic masses, under the domain-group rule) equal the reference values under the numeric tolerance rule, with the same Time (ns) and Frame comparison.

For every frame row, C-alphas, CORE, LID and NMP (residue-number-weighted: alpha-carbon fitting set and domain backbone atoms weighted by resid, under the domain-group rule) equal the reference values under the numeric tolerance rule, with the same Time (ns) and Frame comparison.

The four per-frame tables report the identical Time (ns) value for each frame row (all four tables sample the same trajectory through the same reader convention), up to the absolute 1e-9 time tolerance.

open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv exists at its declared path, its header is exactly 'backbone_rmsd_angstrom' (comma-separated, no index column), and it contains exactly one data row with one finite, unquoted, well-formed value; additional data rows or any malformed content fail.

The single value (unweighted backbone RMSD between trajectory frame 0 and the open-conformation reference structure after centroid subtraction and optimal rotation) equals the reference value under the numeric tolerance rule above.

instruction:
# Acceptance rules (addendum to the task specification)

The grading compares five CSV files read at the declared output paths (`backbone_rmsd.csv`, `core_ca_rmsd.csv`, `mass_weighted_rmsd.csv`, `resid_weighted_rmsd.csv`, `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv`), each relative to the submission output root. Files placed elsewhere (for example under an additional nested output directory) are not found and fail.

## Format conventions

- Each file is plain comma-separated text with exactly one header row and no index column. The header must match the specification exactly (same column names, same order). Ragged rows, quoted numbers, empty/missing fields, nonfinite values (NaN/Inf), non-numeric text, surrounding whitespace within fields, NUL bytes and duplicate header names all fail.
- Outputs 1–4 contain exactly one data row per trajectory frame, ordered by increasing 0-based frame index and covering every frame of the supplied trajectory without omissions, duplicates or extra rows. The `Frame` column equals the 0-based row position (integer-valued; writing `7` or `7.0` are both accepted since only the parsed value is compared).
- `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv` has exactly one data row containing the single RMSD value.
- Values are compared numerically after parsing. Writing numbers in any fixed, scientific or shortest-round-trip notation is acceptable at full precision; rounding that loses scientific precision beyond the tolerances below fails.

## Numeric comparison rules

- For each RMSD column, the submitted value `s` is accepted relative to the reference value `r` when `|s - r| <= max(3e-6 Å, 1e-9 · |r|)`, with the reference value as denominator. The 3e-6 Å absolute floor covers both frame-0 self-comparison values (which legitimately sit near zero) and coordinate-storage/serialization rounding for Å-scale values; the 1e-9 relative tail is a guard for arbitrarily large values only.
- `Time (ns)` holds the reader-assigned per-frame time value and is compared absolutely at 1e-9 (both accepted implementations produce bit-identical frame times for this trajectory). It is a required column with real scientific content; it is not free-form.
- All five outputs must agree with the reference, i.e. membership plus multiplicity per frame row; subsets, permuted rows or added unsupported rows are rejected. Row alignment uses the `Frame` column (not file order alone).
- Nonfinite (NaN/Inf), missing or unparseable numbers fail the corresponding check even where a tolerance would otherwise apply; negative RMSDs fail by value comparison.

## Cross-file consistency

The four per-frame tables report the same trajectory and must carry the identical `Time (ns)` value for each frame. The RMSD columns themselves are different scientific quantities per file and are compared only against their same-named counterpart in the same file at the same frame row.
rationale:
## Scientific target and scope
Five endpoints, all specified in the approved public question: per-frame unweighted backbone/CORE/LID/NMP RMSD after unweighted global backbone fit; CORE alpha-carbon RMSD (self superposition); mass-weighted RMSD (CA fit + weighted domain groups); residue-number-weighted RMSD (same construction); and the single open-vs-closed backbone RMSD (computation 5). The two former endpoints were recovered by source-faithful recomputation of unchanged notebook calls (verified deterministic at construction time); three remain the recorded append-only exports.

## Evidence used for the numeric rules
Executed records available to me: the MDAnalysis-2.11.0 reference outputs, an independent construction-run recomputation, and an independently executed alternative implementation (float64 NumPy Kabsch, QCP-equivalent rotation, correct determinant handling) that never had access to the reference values. I diffed all 5 files cell by cell (reference vs alternative):
- `Time (ns)`: bit-identical in both implementations. Source: MDAnalysis DCDReader assigns time from the file header `delta` (0.020454827696084976 AKMA ps) with 48 steps/frame, 1-based (1.0 ... 98.0 observed); this is a reader convention on a timestamp-free DCD, so I compare it absolutely (1e-9), matching the public question's wording, not as physics.
- Fitting-set RMSD columns: max |diff| ~2.6e-14 Å (pure double-precision arithmetic agreement).
- Domain-group columns (no-refit after global fit): max |diff| ~1.5e-6 Å. Cause: the reference path (MDAnalysis RMSD groups) keeps coordinates in the file's float32 storage representation, and 32-bit coordinate rounding (~6e-8 relative on ~200-coordinate Å displacements) propagates into the post-fit domain displacements; the alternative path lifts to float64 earlier. This is real storage-representation noise, not a methodological difference.
- Frame-0 self-RMSD: reference ~1e-7 Å (float32 QCP path) vs ~1e-15 Å (true zero). Any absolute tolerance below ~1e-7 would reject a mathematically exact answer; a float32-precision-based tolerance must sit above ~1.5e-6.

Therefore the RMSD rule is |s−r| ≤ max(3e-6 Å, 1e-9·|r|), reference value as denominator, boundary inclusive. Rationale: 3e-6 Å = 2× the worst measured implementation discrepancy (1.5e-6 Å) covering both frame-0 noise windows and general float32 storage effects, tight enough that a wrong method (observed magnitudes: per-domain refit ≈0.03–0.1 Å, unweighted-instead-of-mass-weighted ≈1.3e-3 Å and larger, wrong reference frame, wrong fitting set, wrong domain definitions, charges-instead-of-resids) is rejected by orders of magnitude. The 1e-9 relative tail only engages |r| > 3 Å, ~5× larger than the 7e-10 observed double-precision reproducibility of such values, and cannot weaken the absolute floor. I verified the boundary in local tests: +2e-6 Å accepted, +4e-6 Å rejected, a 5e-6 single-cell edit rejected at both the structural and scientific check.

## Comparison design
- Row alignment via the 0-based Frame column; row count must equal the reference count (one row per frame, membership + multiplicity); permuted rows fail (Frame vs row-position check).
- Time column is compared per file and additionally cross-checked for identity across the four per-frame tables (they sample the same trajectory).
- Sub-1e-7 frame-0 self-values cannot distinguish the reference's float32-derived non-zero noise from an exact 0; this residual distinction is representation-level and the 3e-6 floor absorbs it. No other normalization was introduced; no hashes, no embedded answers; the grader reads reference values dynamically.
- Rejects nonfinite/NaN/Inf, empty and unparseable fields explicitly; requires exact single-row schema for the static endpoint; verifies all 8 checks are emitted for empty submissions.
- Checks parsed content only; software choice stays open (the alternative toolchain passes).

## Local verification performed (evidence, not acceptance)
Reference self-compare passes; empty submission fails all 8 checks; missing-file cases fail; mutant submissions (single-cell value shift, systematic domain column shift emulating per-domain refit, NaN injection, row swap, static value shift, extra nested output directory) all fail with failures confined to the affected checks; boundary values behave as stated.

## Limitations
Frame-0 self-comparison window (above) is the only place where representation-level indistinguishability remains; it cannot accept a scientific mutation since those shift values by far more than 3e-6 Å. The tolerance is calibrated from two independent implementations on the same trajectory; additional third-party toolchains would need their own measured agreement evidence. The 1e-9 time tolerance is exact for both observed readers of this DCD convention.
